subject.title: PR5/5 durable core: internal session delivery handoff

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this opt-in durable-runtime schema and wake-to-session-queue ownership model on the 2026.7.1 release line, and should the five-part stack land in its proposed order?
rationale: The PR creates shared persistent state, public Gateway and plugin SDK contracts, and a new recovery semantic where durable delivery completes at internal queue handoff; tests cannot choose those permanent product and upgrade boundaries.

options.title: Approve ordered durable stack
options.body: Accept the architecture, then require immutable CI tooling and exact-head recovery proof before landing each dependency-ordered slice.

options.title: Narrow to restart recovery
options.body: Retain only the smallest session-recovery behavior needed for the open restart issue and defer the general durable runtime, public RPCs, and SDK surface.

options.title: Defer the durable program
options.body: Keep the existing restart continuation queue and close or pause this stack until the broader durable-runtime product direction is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Approve ordered durable stack
recommendation.body: Accept the architecture, then require immutable CI tooling and exact-head recovery proof before landing each dependency-ordered slice.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans the release line, shared database schema, core Gateway protocol, and public plugin contract rather than one isolated implementation module.
